paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: life doesn't always add up, and you can't figure out all of it. The Teacher saw a righteous man perishing and a wicked man living long (Ecclesiastes 7:15). He tried to be wise and said, "But it was beyond me." (Ecclesiastes 7:23). Some things are "out of reach and very deep," and the wisest man in the room still has to say, "Who can fathom it?" (Ecclesiastes 7:24).

So what do you do with a world you can't fully figure out? The Teacher says it is good to hold on to both warnings, and that "he who fears God will follow both warnings." (Ecclesiastes 7:18). He also says, "Surely there is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins." (Ecclesiastes 7:20). I think that's good news for a stamper who spent years blurry in the back of a drawer, because nobody here is a finished cookie, so nobody gets to look down on the one next to them.

And here's the part I want you to carry out of my bakery. The Teacher says, "God made mankind upright, but they have sought out many schemes." (Ecclesiastes 7:29). The problem was never that God made us wrong, it's the schemes we cook up on our own. So bring your hunt for answers to God, keep fearing Him, and let the deep stuff stay deep, friend. You can rest in Him even when you can't see the bottom of the bin.
